title: Haemoglobin is below the reference range
what_it_means: Haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
diet_do: Include ragi, spinach, dates, jaggery and eggs or meat if you eat them; add lemon or amla to iron-rich meals
diet_dont: Avoid tea or coffee within an hour of meals

title: Haemoglobin is above the reference range
what_it_means: Haemoglobin carries oxygen in your blood; a higher value can follow dehydration or smoking.
diet_do: Drink water steadily through the day
diet_dont: Avoid smoking

title: Red blood cell count is below the reference range
what_it_means: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.

title: Red blood cell count is above the reference range
what_it_means: Red blood cells carry oxygen around your body; the count can rise with dehydration or smoking.

title: White blood cell count is below the reference range
what_it_means: White blood cells are part of how your body fights infection.

title: White blood cell count is above the reference range
what_it_means: White blood cells rise while your body is dealing with an infection or inflammation.

title: Platelet count is below the reference range
what_it_means: Platelets are the cells that help your blood clot when you are injured.

title: Platelet count is above the reference range
what_it_means: Platelets help your blood clot; the count can rise for a while after an infection.

title: PCV is below the reference range
what_it_means: PCV is the share of your blood made up of red cells, so it usually moves together with haemoglobin.

title: PCV is above the reference range
what_it_means: PCV is the share of your blood made up of red cells; it can rise when you are dehydrated.

title: Red blood cells are smaller than usual
what_it_means: MCV is the average size of your red blood cells; a low value often travels with a low haemoglobin.

title: Red blood cells are larger than usual
what_it_means: MCV is the average size of your red blood cells; a high value is sometimes linked to vitamin B12 or folate levels.

title: MCH is below the reference range
what_it_means: MCH is the average amount of haemoglobin carried inside each red blood cell.

title: MCH is above the reference range
what_it_means: MCH is the average amount of haemoglobin carried inside each red blood cell.

title: MCHC is below the reference range
what_it_means: MCHC describes how concentrated the haemoglobin is inside your red blood cells.

title: MCHC is above the reference range
what_it_means: MCHC describes how concentrated the haemoglobin is inside your red blood cells.

title: Red cell size varies more than usual
what_it_means: RDW describes how much your red blood cells differ from one another in size.

title: Neutrophils are below the reference range
what_it_means: Neutrophils are the white cells that respond first to bacterial infection.

title: Neutrophils are above the reference range
what_it_means: Neutrophils are the white cells that respond first to bacterial infection.

title: Lymphocytes are below the reference range
what_it_means: Lymphocytes are the white cells involved in fighting viruses and building immunity.

title: Lymphocytes are above the reference range
what_it_means: Lymphocytes are the white cells involved in fighting viruses and building immunity.

title: Eosinophils are above the reference range
what_it_means: Eosinophils are the white cells that rise with allergies and with some parasitic infections.

title: Monocytes are above the reference range
what_it_means: Monocytes are white cells that clear damaged cells and help with longer-running infections.

title: ESR is above the reference range
what_it_means: ESR is a general marker that rises when there is inflammation somewhere in the body.

title: Fasting blood sugar is above the reference range
what_it_means: This is your blood sugar after an overnight fast, so it shows how your body handles sugar at rest.
diet_do: Swap white rice for hand-pounded or brown rice, or mix in millets
diet_dont: Avoid sugary tea, coffee and bakery items
lifestyle: Aim for 30 minutes of activity on most days

title: Fasting blood sugar is below the reference range
what_it_means: This is your blood sugar after an overnight fast; a low value can follow a long gap between meals.
diet_do: Eat at regular intervals and carry a small snack
diet_dont: Avoid skipping meals

title: Post-meal blood sugar is above the reference range
what_it_means: This is your blood sugar about two hours after a meal, which shows how well your body clears sugar after eating.
diet_do: Eat vegetables or dal before the rice portion of a meal
diet_dont: Avoid sweets and sweetened drinks
lifestyle: Take a 10-minute walk after each main meal

title: Random blood sugar is above the reference range
what_it_means: This is a blood sugar reading taken without fasting, so it varies with what you last ate.

title: Your three-month average sugar is above range
what_it_means: HbA1c reflects your average blood sugar over roughly the last three months, so it is less affected by what you ate yesterday.
diet_do: Eat vegetables or dal before the rice portion of a meal
diet_dont: Avoid sweets, sweetened drinks and fruit juice
lifestyle: Aim for 30 minutes of activity on most days

title: Total cholesterol is above the recommended range
what_it_means: This is the sum of all the cholesterol carried in your blood.
diet_do: Add oats, whole dals and rajma; keep cooking oil to 3-4 teaspoons a day
diet_dont: Limit fried foods and bakery items
lifestyle: Aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking on most days

title: LDL cholesterol is above the recommended range
what_it_means: LDL is the cholesterol that can build up in the walls of your blood vessels over time.
diet_do: Add oats, whole dals and rajma; keep cooking oil to 3-4 teaspoons a day
diet_dont: Limit fried foods like samosas, pakoras and bakery items
lifestyle: Aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking on most days

title: HDL cholesterol is below the recommended range
what_it_means: HDL carries cholesterol away from your blood vessels, so a higher number is the better one here.
diet_do: Include nuts, seeds and cold-pressed oils in small amounts
diet_dont: Avoid trans fats and vanaspati
lifestyle: Add 30 minutes of brisk activity on most days

title: Triglycerides are above the recommended range
what_it_means: Triglycerides are the fats your body stores for energy; they rise with refined carbohydrates, sugar and alcohol.
diet_do: Choose whole grains and millets over white rice and maida
diet_dont: Limit alcohol and sweetened drinks
lifestyle: Walk for 10 minutes after each main meal

title: VLDL cholesterol is above the recommended range
what_it_means: VLDL is the particle that carries triglycerides in your blood, so it tends to rise along with them.

title: Cholesterol to HDL ratio is above the recommended range
what_it_means: This ratio compares your total cholesterol with the protective HDL fraction.

title: SGPT / ALT is above the reference range
what_it_means: ALT is an enzyme released by liver cells and is one of the standard measures of how the liver is doing.
diet_do: Choose home-cooked meals and cut down on fried and processed food
diet_dont: Avoid alcohol until your doctor advises otherwise
lifestyle: Aim for gradual weight reduction if your doctor advises it

title: SGOT / AST is above the reference range
what_it_means: AST is an enzyme found in the liver and also in muscle, so it is read alongside ALT.
diet_do: Choose home-cooked meals and cut down on fried and processed food
diet_dont: Avoid alcohol until your doctor advises otherwise

title: Alkaline phosphatase is above the reference range
what_it_means: ALP is an enzyme that comes mainly from the liver and from bone.

title: GGT is above the reference range
what_it_means: GGT is a liver enzyme that is particularly sensitive to alcohol and to some medicines.
diet_dont: Avoid alcohol until your doctor advises otherwise

title: Total bilirubin is above the reference range
what_it_means: Bilirubin is a pigment your liver clears from the blood after old red cells break down.

title: Direct bilirubin is above the reference range
what_it_means: Direct bilirubin is the fraction of bilirubin your liver has already processed.

title: Total protein is below the reference range
what_it_means: Total protein is the combined measure of albumin and globulin in your blood.

title: Albumin is below the reference range
what_it_means: Albumin is the main protein your liver makes; it helps hold fluid inside your blood vessels.

title: Globulin is above the reference range
what_it_means: Globulins are the blood proteins involved in immunity and in transporting substances around the body.

title: Albumin to globulin ratio is below the reference range
what_it_means: This ratio compares the two main groups of protein in your blood.

title: Creatinine is above the reference range
what_it_means: Creatinine is a waste product from muscle that your kidneys filter out of the blood.
diet_do: Drink water steadily through the day
diet_dont: Avoid over-the-counter painkillers unless your doctor has prescribed them

title: Blood urea is above the reference range
what_it_means: Urea is a waste product from protein that your kidneys clear from the blood.

title: BUN is above the reference range
what_it_means: BUN is another way of reporting the urea that your kidneys clear.

title: Uric acid is above the reference range
what_it_means: Uric acid is a waste product your kidneys clear; over time a high level can settle in joints.
diet_do: Drink more water through the day
diet_dont: Cut down on organ meats, red meat, shellfish and beer

title: eGFR is below the reference range
what_it_means: eGFR is an estimate of how well your kidneys are filtering your blood.

title: Sodium is below the reference range
what_it_means: Sodium is one of the salts that keeps the fluid balance in your body steady.

title: Sodium is above the reference range
what_it_means: Sodium is one of the salts that keeps the fluid balance in your body steady.

title: Potassium is below the reference range
what_it_means: Potassium is a salt that matters for how your muscles and heart rhythm work.

title: Potassium is above the reference range
what_it_means: Potassium is a salt that matters for how your muscles and heart rhythm work.

title: Chloride is below the reference range
what_it_means: Chloride works alongside sodium to keep your body's fluid balance steady.

title: Chloride is above the reference range
what_it_means: Chloride works alongside sodium to keep your body's fluid balance steady.

title: Calcium is below the reference range
what_it_means: Calcium matters for your bones, your muscles and the way your nerves send signals.
diet_do: Include milk, curd, ragi and green leafy vegetables
lifestyle: Get some morning sunlight, which helps your body use calcium

title: Calcium is above the reference range
what_it_means: Calcium matters for your bones, muscles and nerve signals; a raised level is worth a closer look.
diet_do: Drink water regularly through the day
diet_dont: Avoid calcium or vitamin D supplements unless they were prescribed

title: TSH is above the reference range
what_it_means: TSH is the signal your brain sends to your thyroid gland; it rises when the gland is working harder than usual.

title: TSH is below the reference range
what_it_means: TSH is the signal your brain sends to your thyroid gland; it falls when the gland is producing more hormone than usual.

title: T3 is below the reference range
what_it_means: T3 is one of the two main thyroid hormones that set the pace of your metabolism.

title: T3 is above the reference range
what_it_means: T3 is one of the two main thyroid hormones that set the pace of your metabolism.

title: T4 is below the reference range
what_it_means: T4 is the main hormone your thyroid releases, which your body converts into the active form.

title: T4 is above the reference range
what_it_means: T4 is the main hormone your thyroid releases, which your body converts into the active form.

title: Free T3 is below the reference range
what_it_means: Free T3 is the portion of T3 circulating in your blood that is available for your body to use.

title: Free T3 is above the reference range
what_it_means: Free T3 is the portion of T3 circulating in your blood that is available for your body to use.

title: Free T4 is below the reference range
what_it_means: Free T4 is the portion of T4 in your blood that is available for your body to use.

title: Free T4 is above the reference range
what_it_means: Free T4 is the portion of T4 in your blood that is available for your body to use.

title: Vitamin D is below the reference range
what_it_means: Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium and keeps bones and muscles working well.
diet_do: Add fortified milk, eggs and mushrooms
diet_dont: Do not start a vitamin D supplement on your own without advice
lifestyle: Get 15-20 minutes of morning sunlight on your arms and face most days

title: Vitamin D is above the reference range
what_it_means: Vitamin D is usually high because of supplements rather than food or sunlight.
diet_dont: Do not continue a vitamin D supplement without checking with your doctor

title: Vitamin B12 is below the reference range
what_it_means: B12 is needed to make healthy red blood cells and to keep your nerves working well.
diet_do: Include milk, curd, paneer, eggs, fish or meat if you eat them

title: Vitamin B12 is above the reference range
what_it_means: A high B12 is most often the result of supplements or injections rather than diet.
diet_dont: Mention any B12 supplement or injection to your doctor

title: Folate is below the reference range
what_it_means: Folate works together with vitamin B12 to make healthy red blood cells.
diet_do: Include dark green leafy vegetables, dals and citrus fruit

title: Serum iron is below the reference range
what_it_means: Serum iron is the iron circulating in your blood at the moment the sample was taken.
diet_do: Include ragi, dates, jaggery, beans and lentils; add lemon or amla to meals
diet_dont: Avoid tea and coffee with meals

title: Serum iron is above the reference range
what_it_means: Serum iron is the iron circulating in your blood at the moment the sample was taken.
diet_dont: Avoid iron supplements unless they were prescribed

title: Ferritin is below the reference range
what_it_means: Ferritin reflects the iron your body has in store, so it falls before haemoglobin does.
diet_do: Include ragi, dates, jaggery, beans and lentils; add lemon or amla to meals
diet_dont: Avoid tea and coffee with meals

title: Ferritin is above the reference range
what_it_means: Ferritin reflects your stored iron, but it also rises when there is inflammation in the body.
diet_dont: Avoid iron supplements unless they were prescribed

title: TIBC is above the reference range
what_it_means: TIBC measures how much more iron your blood could carry, and it rises when stores are low.

title: TIBC is below the reference range
what_it_means: TIBC measures how much more iron your blood could carry.

title: Transferrin saturation is below the reference range
what_it_means: This is the share of your blood's iron-carrying capacity that is actually filled.

title: CRP is above the reference range
what_it_means: CRP is a general marker that rises when there is inflammation somewhere in the body.

title: PSA is above the reference range
what_it_means: PSA is a protein made by the prostate gland; the level rises for several reasons and needs a doctor's interpretation.

title: Total testosterone is below the reference range
what_it_means: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone and also affects muscle mass and energy levels.
